profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the Corporate Strategy team and the Investor Relations team at a regional asset management firm preparing materials for the quarterly investment committee on ASEAN-5 stock market integration. The firm is repackaging an internal research note titled around the ARDL-based revisit of Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines, and Singapore, highlighting that integration strengthened across the pre-1997, post-1997, and post-U.S. subprime periods and that diversification benefits have diminished. The agenda is to align on which source material the deck will draw from, what the core slide pack should contain, who drafts the policy implications section, and what handoff timing is needed before committee circulation. The expected outcome is a shared-seeming plan for Strategy to provide the main analytical materials and for Investor Relations to package and refine them for leadership use.

members.name: Alicia Tan
members.expertise: Executive synthesis, cross-market strategy narratives, and converting technical research into decision-oriented briefing materials
members.background: Alicia spent six years in management consulting before joining the asset manager, where she now coordinates thematic strategy packs for senior leadership across public markets and macro strategy teams.
members.private_state: She wants a clean committee-ready pack with minimal iteration, and she is trying to show that Strategy can independently turn specialist research into leadership materials without getting dragged into communications-process overhead.
hidden_assumptions: When people mention 'the ARDL integration note,' they obviously mean the latest Strategy folder version with the refreshed post-subprime framing and tightened wording on reduced diversification benefits.
A 'core slide pack' for an investment committee means the lean executive set itself, not a source file that must also support later client reuse.
Adding 'policy implications' means a short strategic interpretation for internal leadership, not compliance-sensitive wording for external audiences.
If a pack is 'final by Thursday,' it is already usable for executive pre-read circulation by Thursday afternoon Singapore time, even if design polish continues afterward.

members.name: Marcus Villanueva
members.expertise: Research communications, reusable presentation architecture, and approval workflows for materials that may later face clients or relationship managers
members.background: Marcus previously worked in sell-side equity communications and joined the firm to bridge investment research and distribution, with a focus on making technical market content usable across Southeast Asian client channels.
members.private_state: He wants any material his team touches to be safely reusable outside the committee context, avoid unsupported wording around market-policy conclusions, and prevent his team from being handed a half-built deck too late to run its normal packaging process.
hidden_assumptions: When colleagues refer to 'the ARDL integration note,' they mean the last writing-reviewed version already circulated through the communications channel, because that is the only stable source worth building from.

A 'core slide pack' is the master deck that downstream teams can pull from, so it should already include appendix-ready support, source lines, and methodology backup even if leadership only sees the front section.
Adding 'policy implications' requires careful framing, caveats, and wording that will not read as house policy advice if the content is later reused externally.
If something is 'final by Thursday,' that means content-complete by end of day Thursday so IR can still run formatting and internal checks before any real distribution.

misalignment_points.topic: Which file both think is the ARDL integration note
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to build from 'the ARDL integration note.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Alicia means the latest Strategy-shared December file containing updated language on stronger post-subprime integration and cleaner implications wording.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means the last communications-reviewed draft circulated earlier by email, which has older captions, slightly different conclusion text, and no late wording revisions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The title/topic is stable across versions, so saying 'the ARDL integration note' sounds fully specific even though each person accesses it through a different channel and assumes there is one obvious canonical copy.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the core slide pack
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that Strategy will send over 'the core slide pack.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Alicia means the six-to-eight slide executive sequence for the investment committee: headline findings, one or two cleaned charts, and a concise implications slide, with methods left out unless requested.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means the master deck that contains the executive sequence plus appendix slides, source notes, ARDL-method backup, and citation-ready footnotes so IR can repurpose it without rebuilding.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Unlike 'summary deck,' 'core slide pack' plausibly refers either to the visible leadership section or to the underlying source deck, so each hears a familiar internal term and silently maps it to their own workflow.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as final by Thursday
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both align on having the pack 'final by Thursday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Alicia means ready for Thursday afternoon executive circulation, with only superficial design touch-ups allowed later.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means the substance is locked by Thursday end of day, after which IR still has Friday for formatting cleanup, supporting notes, and internal sign-off before meaningful distribution.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use standard deadline shorthand from their own functions, and because neither names the exact distribution event in the moment, 'final' feels like shared language while hiding different completion thresholds.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to add the policy implications
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that IR will help with 'the policy implications.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Alicia expects Marcus to draft a short internal-facing implications section connecting tighter ASEAN market integration to the need for regional policy coordination and reduced diversification benefits for investors.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus expects his team to translate that section into carefully caveated language with standard framing so it can sit safely in a deck that may later be adapted for external audiences.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They appear aligned on the same section heading and both think IR is simply 'tightening the wording,' but each assumes a different default drafting process based on their own audience norms.
